title: Truncated Impossible Differentials Around ForkSkinny's Forking Point
summary: For ForkSkinny, existing results reach at most 11 rounds in the single-tweakey model and 12, 14, or 16 for TK1, TK2, or TK3; distinguishers around the forking point remain to be studied.

formal_statement.body: For ForkSkinny, study truncated impossible-differential distinguishers positioned around the forking point, a case not covered by the existing results that reach at most 11 rounds in the single-tweakey model and 12, 14, or 16 rounds for TK1, TK2, or TK3 in the related-tweakey setting. In particular, determine the maximum number of rounds covered in the single-tweakey case where the contradiction is formed by one active cell from one direction and one inactive cell from the other direction, and extend the analysis to the related-tweakey settings when applicable.

scope.domain: This is a symmetric-key cryptanalysis problem concerning truncated impossible-differential distinguishers for ForkSkinny.
parameters: tweakey setting: single-tweakey or related-tweakey, including TK1, TK2, and TK3
round count: number of rounds covered by the distinguisher
differential position: around the forking point
cell activity pattern: one active cell from one direction and one inactive cell from the other in the single-tweakey case
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine the maximum round coverage for the truncated impossible-differential case positioned around the ForkSkinny forking point, beginning with the specified single-tweakey contradiction and extending to related-tweakey settings when applicable.

citations.label: Forkcipher: A New Primitive for Authenticated Encryption of Very Short Messages

progress.summary: The source explicitly identifies the around-the-forking-point placement as a case that remains to be studied. It presents the single-tweakey active/inactive-cell case as a first estimate against existing coverage of at most 11 rounds in the single-tweakey model and 12, 14, and 16 rounds for TK1, TK2, and TK3 in related-tweakey settings.
citation_labels: Elena Andreeva et al., Forkcipher: A New Primitive for Authenticated Encryption of Very Short Messages
